name: Encryption at Rest and Key Management Configuration
description: The declared encryption state of in-scope storage together with the key management configuration governing who can use and administer the keys.

expected_content.element: Per-resource encryption status across every in-scope storage class
expected_content.why: Coverage is the substance of the control; a single compliant datastore says nothing about the estate.

expected_content.element: Explicit inclusion of backups, snapshots, replicas, and log archives
expected_content.why: These are the objects most often left unencrypted while primary storage is compliant.

expected_content.element: Algorithm and key length in use
expected_content.why: Encryption enabled with a deprecated algorithm does not meet the objective the control claims.

expected_content.element: Key management configuration: provider-managed or customer-managed, and where keys reside
expected_content.why: Determines what the control actually mitigates.

expected_content.element: Principals able to use keys and principals able to administer them, listed separately
expected_content.why: Encryption provides no separation if the population that reads data also controls the keys.

expected_content.element: Rotation configuration and the date of last rotation
expected_content.why: Supports the rotation element of the control where one is claimed.

expected_content.element: Organisation-level enforcement policy preventing creation of unencrypted storage
expected_content.why: Distinguishes an enforced default from a convention that new resources may not follow.

source_system_examples: Cloud security posture management encryption report

freshness_expectation.rationale: DriftGuard default for a continuously enforced configuration. Not an audit rule.

redaction_guidance: Never include key material, key export blobs, or recovery values.
Key identifiers and policy documents are safe to include and are what the artifact needs.
retention_guidance: Capture on a schedule and retain each dated snapshot alongside EV-CONFIG-001; a single snapshot cannot evidence a period.

validation_rules.rule: An encryption configuration export exists covering in-scope storage.
Every storage resource holding protected information appears, including backups, snapshots, and replicas.
Key use and key administration principals are separately identifiable.
For a Type 2 conclusion the export is paired with EV-CONFIG-001 covering the period.
The export is dated within the examination period or the freshness window.
The artifact is an API export identifying the account or project, not a console screenshot.

common_issues.issue: Primary datastore encrypted while backups and snapshots are not.
common_issues.impact: The most portable copy of the data is the unprotected one.

common_issues.issue: Key administration and application data access held by the same principal.
common_issues.impact: Encryption provides no separation from an application-layer compromise.

common_issues.issue: Single export presented as evidence for a twelve-month period.
common_issues.impact: Point-in-time state cannot support an operating-effectiveness conclusion.

source_refs.supports: Expected content, persuasiveness weighting, and the common issues list.
Freshness window, sensitivity classification, and redaction guidance.

notes: Provider-managed keys are not a deficiency. DriftGuard assesses whether the choice is documented and whether key access is appropriately restricted, not which option was chosen.
